page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r8i.2xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance based on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by a dedicated 2.7 GHz Intel Xeon 8475B processor built on the x86_64 architecture. The instance provides 8 dedicated vCPUs paired with 64.0 GB of memory, yielding a 1:8 compute-to-memory allocation of 8.0 GB RAM per vCPU. Hardware vector, matrix, and cryptographic extensions are not exposed to the guest environment.

The ecs.r8i.2xlarge instance does not include bundled local storage, requiring network-attached block storage volumes for persistent data and operating system installations. It delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 6 Gbps and does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Hardware accelerator support is absent, with zero GPUs present on the instance.

With an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio, the instance is structured to deliver resource efficiency for workloads where memory capacity constraints precede compute requirements. This configuration avoids over-provisioning compute resources while securing substantial memory density. The instance fits in-memory databases, distributed caching tiers, analytics data pipelines, memory-intensive ETL tasks, and relational database servers.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r8i.2xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8475B x86_64 processor operating at 2.7 GHz. Provisioned via the KVM hypervisor, it features 8 dedicated vCPUs and 64.0 GB of system memory, maintaining an 8.0 GB per core ratio. The instance contains no bundled local storage, necessitating reliance on remote cloud block storage for system and application persistence. Network connectivity operates at a baseline throughput of 6 Gbps, and no GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included. Providing high memory density per compute core, the instance minimizes compute overhead for applications constrained primarily by RAM capacity. The ecs.r8i.2xlarge is suitable for in-memory caching platforms, mid-scale relational database engines, memory-intensive ETL tasks, and real-time enterprise analytics.
